column1: Per-negative-class accuracy on the T15 test set (969 positives vs 2354 negatives). Hardest class first.

column2: Number of windows of this negative class in the T15 test set.
Median of the model's 0-1 promoter score over the class. For a negative, lower is better: the model is more confident it is not a promoter.

Fraction of the class the model correctly scored BELOW the 0.5 cutoff (i.e. called non-promoter). This is the true-negative rate for the class at the 0.5 threshold. Higher is better. (This is the column previously labelled 'rejection@0.5'.) It depends on the 0.5 threshold and will shift after T26 calibration.

Probability the model scores a random real promoter above a random window of this class. 1.0 = perfectly separable, 0.5 = chance. Threshold-free and unchanged by calibration, so it is the fairer cross-model comparison.
90% bootstrap confidence interval for the AUROC.

column1: Difficulty order is the same for all three models: Intergenic < SRS < Downstream < CDS.
Intergenic convergent regions (real AT-rich genomic sequence) are the hardest negative, not SRS.
By AUROC: ProkBERT >= NT-LoRA >= CNN on every class. CNN is weakest, especially Intergenic (rejects only 0.681; median score 0.220).
NT-LoRA's higher overall rejection (0.907) is a threshold effect, not better separation; its AUROC is below ProkBERT's on every class.
Only CDS is genuinely easy to reject (0.94-0.98). Intergenic and SRS (0.86-0.92) are where the model does real motif work and where T33 hard-negative mining would help most.
Overall correct-rejection rate across all 2354 negatives: ProkBERT 0.887, NT-LoRA 0.907, CNN 0.804.
